title: The City Inequality Question: What Metropolitan Data Reveals
summary: City-level inequality reveals local differences that national averages conceal, while a coverage audit shows how little of the urban world is measured consistently.
key_takeaway: National averages need a metropolitan lens: two cities under the same national policy can experience genuinely different levels of inequality. But the metropolitan lens itself needs a serious coverage audit, since just two countries supply 91% of the deepest longitudinal sample, before it can support credible comparison. Better city policy begins by seeing the inequality and the blind spots in the measurement at the same time.
